description: Provides a rigorous foundation in the design, asymptotic analysis, and implementation of efficient computational algorithms and advanced data structures to solve complex algorithmic problems.
learning_objectives: Master asymptotic complexity analysis and recurrence relations.
Design and implement advanced data structures including balanced search trees, heaps, and disjoint sets.
Apply core algorithmic paradigms including divide-and-conquer, greedy techniques, dynamic programming, and branch-and-bound.
Implement graph algorithms, network flow, string matching, and understand NP-completeness and approximation algorithms.
outline: Asymptotic Analysis and Recurrence Relations: Big-O, Omega, Theta notations, Master Theorem, recursion tree method.
Advanced Data Structures: AVL trees, Red-Black trees, B-Trees, Fibonacci heaps, Disjoint Set Union (DSU).
Algorithmic Paradigms: Divide and Conquer, Greedy Algorithms, Dynamic Programming (memoization & tabulation), Backtracking, Branch and Bound.
Graph Algorithms: Single-source and all-pairs shortest paths (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall), Minimum Spanning Trees (Prim, Kruskal), Maximum Flow (Ford-Fulkerson).
String Matching Algorithms: Naive, Rabin-Karp, Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP), Boyer-Moore, Suffix Trees.
Computational Complexity: Class P, NP, NP-Complete, NP-Hard, Polynomial-time reductions, Approximation algorithms.
Lab Component: Practical implementation and performance benchmarking in C++/Python.
